judged_text: SalesforceCalendarService construction now unconditionally performs a live token refresh against login.salesforce.com plus a credential DB write on every instantiation, where previously it built jsforce.Connection from the stored key and let jsforce refresh lazily. Every Salesforce calendar operation gains a Salesforce OAuth round-trip and a DB write (inviting rate limiting or refresh-token lockout), and a transient refresh failure now throws HttpError 400 before any operation even when the stored access token was still valid — previously-working Salesforce installs start failing on network blips, a default-path behavior change unrelated to the credential-sync opt-in.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, new code unconditionally performs a refresh-token HTTP POST to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` and then `prisma.credential.update(...)` before returning a `jsforce.Connection` (see added block starting with `const response = await fetch(...)` and subsequent DB update). This makes every instantiation depend on a live Salesforce round-trip and triggers a DB write even if the stored access token is still valid. It also now throws early (`if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, ... })`) on transient failures, which can break previously-working operations. This behavior is not gated by `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` / sync endpoint, so it affects the default path.
